Millwall vs West Ham recap: Six arrests after spitting incident and red card in heated clash
Millwall and West Ham went head-to-head in their first match for 14 years, as they played out a feisty encounter at The Den with a number of measures taken by authorities
The Met have deployed 400 police officers for the clash(Image: Steven Paston/PA Wire)

Sport
Scott Trotter Sports Writer and Mark Wakefield Sport Central Audience Writer
Updated 18:59, 19 Sep 2026

Welcome to Mirror Football’s coverage of the Championship clash between Millwall and West Ham, amid fears of violence in the capital.
The Lions hosted the Hammers at the Den on Saturday afternoon as the teams faced off for the first time since 2012. Millwall looked more prepared from the first whistle as a lively atmosphere got the clash underway.

Police issued a Section 35 dispersal order, which will be in place on Saturday because of the match between Millwall and West Ham, and will impact a large percentage of London.
They also implemented a Section 60 order which offered them greater stop and search powers of individuals and vehicles until 8pm.

Nuno on Taty spit allegation
The West Ham boss says he did not see the incident.
I didn't see it so I'm not going to comment on any allegations. That is not what we should speak about for this game, it was an intense game for both fans.

Nuno Espirito Santo has given his verdict.
The first half was not the way we wanted. We did not start the game well. We didn't do the physical part of the game. We didn't do well. Much improved in the second half and positive the way the game went.

It's only a free kick and Millwall can't capitalise.

Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall receives a warning after holding onto the ball for 11 seconds. West Ham think they've won a corner and Pablo taps the ball in as they react.

Still two goals clear with just over 20 minutes remaining now.
